test.name: Wikipedia request must not trigger a FamilySearch-wiki search
test.description: User explicitly names Wikipedia. That is search-wikipedia (or, for an off-topic subject, a decline), not search-familysearch-wiki. The two skills target different sources — Wikipedia is the general encyclopedia, the FamilySearch Research Wiki is the genealogy-method reference. search-familysearch-wiki must not answer a Wikipedia request by running its own wiki_search.

input.user_message: Look up Albert Einstein on Wikipedia and save the summary

negative.explanation: The user explicitly named Wikipedia — that is search-wikipedia's territory (it calls wikipedia_search), not search-familysearch-wiki's (which calls wiki_search). The routing-independent invariant this test enforces is that search-familysearch-wiki must NOT run its own FamilySearch-wiki search on a Wikipedia request, gated deterministically by the tag-gated validator test_no_spurious_wiki_search (eval/harness/validators/test_search_familysearch_wiki.py, no-wiki-search tag), which fails the run if wiki_search is invoked. Graded via grade_on_invariant because the acceptable no-harm behaviors all leave search-familysearch-wiki out: the router may route to search-wikipedia, OR decline (the observed behavior — Albert Einstein is not a genealogy subject, so a genealogy assistant declining the off-topic request is defensible). correct_skill: ['search-wikipedia'] is retained as documentation of the ideal route, but the invariant is what actually gates; the original routing gate failed the defensible decline path even though search-familysearch-wiki did the right thing by staying out.

judge_context: search-familysearch-wiki should NOT run a FamilySearch-wiki search (wiki_search) on a Wikipedia request
Routing to search-wikipedia OR declining an off-topic Wikipedia lookup are both acceptable; neither should be scored as search-familysearch-wiki mis-handling the request
